items.title: There Really Is No Escape From The Duolingo Owl, Who Will Soon Join Pokémon Go
items.excerpt: Not content with plaguing your phone's lock screen, Duo the Duolingo owl is next set to appear in Pokémon Go.
items.content_text: Not content with plaguing your phone's lock screen, Duo the Duolingo owl is next set to appear in Pokémon Go . A crossover between the two hugely-popular smartphone apps has been announced, unlocking bonuses for players in both experiences. (Sadly, no, you won't be able to trap Duo in a Pokéball forever.) The fun begins on November 17, when a time-limited event begins in Duolingo that requires you to complete at least one language lesson on seven separate days. This will then unlock a series of Pokémon-themed outfits for your Duolingo profile. Completing all of that will also grant a promo code for Pokémon Go, unlocking timed research that awards Pokémon such as Pikachu and regional exclusive Chatot with a unique Duolingo background. It's rather cute — even if it does feature more of Duo the owl, too. Why is all of this happening? While Pokémon Go has featured sponsored cosmetic items in the past, the game rarely offers this level of collaboration, and particularly not with another smartphone app. Still, earlier this year, the game also partnered with LEGO to offer similar bonus gameplay, centered around LEGO stores. More prescient, perhaps, is the rollout of a new feature within Pokémon Go that will allow players to view the name of their creatures in multiple languages for the first time. While Pikachu is known as Pikachu the world over, other species have some very different names on foreign shores. (Snorlax is "Relaxo" in German, for example.) And finally, in other Pokémon Go collaboration news, the creature catching app will soon feature a crossover with Crocs, the shoe brand that already offers a range of Pokémon clogs. All players can now unlock a virtual pair of Pikachu shoes by entering the promo code "POKEMONGOxCROCSxELECTRIFYING". Owners of the real-life Gengar and Jigglypuff shoes, meanwhile, will get codes for similar virtual versions of their own footwear.
items.title_en: There Really Is No Escape From The Duolingo Owl, Who Will Soon Join Pokémon Go

items.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Re-Release With New Footage Sets December Release Date, Tickets on Sale This Week
items.excerpt: Marvel Studios has revealed the release date for its Spider-Man: Brand New Day re-release, promising to bring new footage "and a couple more surprises" to theaters this December.
items.content_text: Marvel Studios has revealed the release date for its Spider-Man: Brand New Day re-release, promising to bring new footage "and a couple more surprises" to theaters this December. The official Spider-Man X/Twitter account confirmed plans to bring Peter Parker's (Tom Holland) first run-in with Jean Grey (Sadie Sink) back to moviegoers when the re-release arrives December 4, 2026. That means we're just a few weeks away from its premiere, with the full post teasing that this version of the movie is "an extended cut featuring new scenes and a couple more surprises." Tickets go on sale this Thursday, November 19. Hope you're not busy! As reported by Deadline earlier this year, Sony had plans to bring Spider-Man: Brand New Day back to theaters just months after the MCU movie's original premiere shattered records . Officially titled Spider-Man: Brand New Brand New Day, the outlet reported today that the plan is still for at least some of that new footage to include a cut scene featuring Rosario Dawson as her Defenders-era character, Night Nurse . Even if you've had your fill of Holland's web-swinging antics for the year, Disney, Marvel, and Sony definitely know what they're doing when it comes to convincing MCU fans for a second round of their movies. Avengers: Doomsday will premiere just two weeks after Spidey returns. Although the December re-release may not be quite as likely to include any tie-in teaser footage like September's Avengers: Endgame Encore , Marvel fans will probably show up just to make sure, especially considering that "couple more surprises" tease. There's also the fact that the wait for Avengers: Doomsday has already been quite long. Marvel has refrained from saying or showing too much about the film's actual plot, making that early December window a nice opportunity to capitalize on the hype and move Spider-Man's box-office needle just a little more. Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiered July 31, 2026, and was immediately a box office hit. It finally arrived on digital October 6 after grossing more than $2.5 billion worldwide, securing its place as one of the highest-grossing movies of all time. IGN gave it a 7/10 review . At the time, we said it "effectively refocuses on the most reliable pillars of the webslinger: battling inner turmoil, swinging around NYC saving the day, and looking cool while doing so.

items.title: The "Next James Bond" Actors Who Never Played James Bond
items.excerpt: While there have only been seven actors to have been officially cast as 007, there have been dozens the media has erroneously labeled as “the next James Bond.”
items.content_text: This article was originally published in August 2018. It has been updated with the latest information. It's been five years since No Time to Die, Daniel Craig's final James Bond film, was released and we finally officially know for certain who his successor is for the role of 007: Robert Pattinson . Even before Craig stepped down, the rumor mill was in overdrive speculating about who would succeed him in the role of 007. This has been a media tradition throughout the franchise’s long history ever since Sean Connery retired his license to kill. But while there have only been now seven actors to (officially) play 007 onscreen, there have been dozens that the media has erroneously labeled as being “the next James Bond.” For the purposes of this feature not running longer than SPECTRE, we’re going to just narrow it down to those actors most often reported as “the next James Bond” in the Daniel Craig era, starting from the time Pierce Brosnan exited the franchise in 2002 until the present. Here then are all the actors who had been pegged as the Next James Bond … and who never ended up playing Bond (well, not yet anyway). Nicholas Hoult James Bond is the second major role that we know of that Hoult has lost out on to Robert Pattinson, the first being the title role in Matt Reeves' The Batman. Hoult wound up getting cast as Lex Luthor in James Gunn's Superman, although we'll have to see now if Hoult will stick around as Lex after Man of Tomorrow comes out in the wake of Gunn's exit from DC Studios. Callum Turner The Fantastic Beasts, Masters of the Air, and One Night Only actor seemed like the front runner to star in James Bond 26 when word spread of the screen tests for director Denis Villeneuve. Turner also seemed like he had the edge given that his wife is pop star Dua Lipa, who could've also done the movie's theme song. But it wasn't meant to be. Jack Lowden The Slow Horses star's passionate fanbase campaigned hard for Lowden, as did his co-star Gary Oldman, but in the end Robert Pattinson prevailed. Josh O'Connor O'Connor starred opposite Daniel Craig in the Knives Out sequel Wake Up, Dead Man, who told IGN he started the rumor about O'Connor being up for the Bond role just to annoy him while doing press. But O'Connor still ended up screen-testing for the role, ultimately losing out to Pattinson. Jack O'Connell The Sinners and Ink actor's name was brought up in recent reports as being a contender for 007 but, as far as we know, he never screen-tested for the role. Jacob Elordi The Frankenstein, Euphoria and Wuthering Heights star was widely seen as a leading and bankable contender for the role, but whether or not he ever seriously considered the role or was formally offered it remains unclear. Aaron Taylor-Johnson The Nosferatu, Kraven the Hunter and Werwulf actor had been the subject of Bond casting buzz going back to before EON Productions parted ways with the franchise. His name seemed to disappear from being in contention once the new producers and Amazon MGM Studios came aboard. Tom Holland Was the Spider-Man star ever truly up for the role or was it all just rumor-mongering by the press? Holland always did seem a bit too young and too short for the role. Idris Elba The Dark Tower and Thor actor’s name resurfaced recently as Daniel Craig’s successor, something the actor already called “a very old rumor” way back in 2011 ! "I would do it, but I don't want to be called the first black James Bond. Do you understand what I'm saying? Sean Connery wasn't the Scottish James Bond and Daniel Craig wasn't the blue-eyed James Bond. So if I played him, I don't want to be called the black James Bond,” Elba said in 2011. "If [then Bond distributor] Sony decided to call me and said hey, we wanted to do [James Bond], I'd definitely consider it." (Note: Sony is no longer the distributor of the Bond movies and it will be the producers’ not the distributor’s call on who plays 007.) Many fans certainly want Elba for the role, but they have also said the same thing about … Tom Hardy The Fury Road and Venom star’s name has come up many times through the years, most often in association with director Christopher Nolan, an avowed Bond fan who has made no secret of his desire to direct a Bond film. While Nolan and Hardy already made their own Bond-esque film with Inception, Hardy was linked with the role again as recently as July 2018. Hardy, for his part, has made cheeky comments about the rumors in interviews and on social media . Time will tell if Hardy ever takes on the secret agent. Tom Hiddleston The Loki actor has made no secret of his desire to play Bond. The rumors really heated up in 2016 when he reportedly met with EON Productions about the role . Of course, the producers could have just been meeting with Hiddleston as leverage against a then-reluctant to return Daniel Craig. In any case, Bond producer Barbara Broccoli reportedly thought Hiddleston wasn’t tough enough for the role, and Daniel Craig eventually signed on for Bond 25. Henry Cavill The Henry Cavill-James Bond rumor was actually legit at one point. The Superman star was the runner-up for the role back when Casino Royale was being cast but, then at only age 23, he lost out to Daniel Craig. Cavill, however, has made absolutely no secret about still wanting the role, reiterating his interest in it as recently as the Mission: Impossible - Fallout press tour, telling Yahoo! , “I would love to do it of course. I think Bond would be a really fun role. It’s British, it’s cool. I think that now that I have my Mission: Impossible badge we can do real stunts and really amp it up as well.” Clive Owen Long before Idris Elba was the actor everyone seemed to believe was the inevitable choice as the next James Bond there was Clive Owen. The actor’s tuxedo-clad turn in the late ‘90s film Croupier kicked off years’ worth of rumor-mongering that he would succeed Pierce Brosnan as 007. Even now, at age 53, Owen still gets asked about the chances he’ll be the next James Bond despite having said he was never even offered the role to begin with. Hugh Jackman The Wolverine actor was rumored for the role quite a bit during the 2000s, but last year he admitted to Variety that he’d actually turned down the part years earlier: “I was about to do X-Men 2 and a call came from my agent asking if I’d be interested in Bond. I just felt at the time that the scripts had become so unbelievable and crazy, and I felt like they needed to become grittier and real. And the response was: ‘Oh, you don’t get a say. You just have to sign on.’ I was also worried that between Bond and X-Men, I’d never have time to do different things.” The timing of Jackman’s approach would have coincided with the release of Pierce Brosnan’s final Bond film, Die Another Day, in 2002. Damian Lewis The Billions actor has been a reported “next James Bond” since his days on Homeland, with bookies reportedly naming him the odds-on favorite for the role back in 2015. When asked about the rumors in 2017, Lewis quipped, “By the time they make a decision [on Bond] I’ll be dead. … So no one need worry any more.” Michael Fassbender While the X-Men and Prometheus actor had long been rumored as Daniel Craig’s successor, he essentially ruled himself out of the running in a 2016 interview : “No, I think the franchise needs something new." Fassbender praised Craig for having done “a cracking job” with the role. Dan Stevens The Beauty and the Beast star was first linked with the role back during his Downton Abbey days, but it was his lean, mean, butt-kicking turn in The Guest that led the press to proclaim him “the next James Bond.” But then Daniel Craig signed back on for one more go as 007 … Eric Bana The Aussie actor, who parlayed his acclaimed turn in the true crime flick Chopper into lead roles in Hulk and Troy, was a reported frontrunner to succeed Pierce Brosnan after Die Another Day. Bana repeatedly denied the rumors back in 2004, and his co-star in Munich, Daniel Craig, won the role in the 2006 reboot Casino Royale. Ewan McGregor The Star Wars and Trainspotting actor reportedly turned down the role of 007 back when Casino Royale was gearing up, but his views on the opportunity have evolved since then. "I think it would be quite cool to play James Bond," McGregor told The Hollywood Reporter in 2015. "At this stage in my career (being typecast) is not really an issue anymore. Early on, when you start off you don't want your horizons to be narrow, but I think people know I have some kind of width in my work, so I'm really not worried about that anymore." Julian McMahon The late Doctor Doom and Nip/Tuck actor said back in 2004 that he’d been “in talks” for the role but later reportedly passed on the role due to his TV commitments. Sam Worthington Before he starred in the highest-grossing movie of all time, Avatar, Worthington was one of the reported finalists who did costumed screen tests for Casino Royale along with Daniel Craig and Henry Cavill. Christian Bale Bale’s name first surfaced in 2002 as a possible replacement for Pierce Brosnan, with the actor reportedly saying at a convention that he’d be open to playing the role. In 2014, however, Bale shot down old reports that he was offered the role before Daniel Craig. Goran Višnjić The Croatian native and ER actor screen-tested back in 2005 for Casino Royale and was reportedly a favorite of director Martin Campbell’s. The role went to Daniel Craig, of course. Rory McCann Long before playing Sandor “The Hound” Clegane on Game of Thrones, the Scottish actor reportedly screen-tested for the role of Bond back in 2005 for Casino Royale. Jamie Bell The Fantastic Four and Turn actor made headlines as a Bond contender in 2016 when he reportedly met with producer Barbara Broccoli about the role. Broccoli and Bell were making the movie Film Stars Don't Die in Liverpool at the time, and the producer was said to have been a fan of Bell’s for sometime. Luke Evans Dan Stevens isn’t the only Beauty and the Beast star who’s been linked as a frontrunner for the role. Luke Evans was reportedly on the shortlist to replace Daniel Craig in 2016 before the latter signed on for one last film. Aidan Turner The Poldark star reportedly had preliminary meetings with Bond producers back in 2016. After Daniel Craig ended up agreeing to return for Bond 25, Turner informed the British press in 2018, “There’s someone else playing the role at the moment, but when it’s free I’ll have a look at it.” James Norton The McMafia and Happy Valley actor was reportedly eyed for the role back in 2016 before Craig signed on for Bond 25. Norton told the press in July 2018, “I would love to play a Bond villain. I love Daniel Craig and I’d love him to do more films. He’s brought a whole other angle to the character — and long may that continue. But people love to speculate.” Alex O'Loughlin The star of Hawaii 5-0 and Man-Thing (yes, there was a TV movie based on the Marvel comic) told the press he did a full costume screen test for Casino Royale but that he was probably too young for the role at the time. Gerard Butler The 300 star has fielded countless questions through the years about possibly playing James Bond, ultimately telling the press in 2009 that he wasn’t interested in the part: “I enjoy doing an array of films. If I was to play Bond, that would quickly stop. How likely would I be accepted doing those roles after having played Bond?" Butler later accepted roles in Geostorm and Gods of Egypt. Jude Law The Sherlock Holmes and future Captain Marvel actor was a much talked about contender back in the early 2000s before Daniel Craig took on the role in Casino Royale. "To be really honest, I don`t know if it`s for me," Law said of the role in 2003. Dougray Scott The Mission: Impossible 2 actor confirmed in a 2004 interview that years of Bond rumors were true. Scott said he was approached for the role back when it looked like Pierce Brosnan was going to bail on the franchise but then he decided to do one last Bond film with Die Another Day. James Purefoy The Following and Rome actor was an oft-reported Bond contender years ago, first for GoldenEye and later Casino Royale. Purefoy said in a 2006 interview that he blew his audition for Casino Royale, believing the producers probably saw him as “Brosnan Lite”. So who’s your favorite “next James Bond” contender? Let us know in the comments. And for more on actors who almost played iconic genre roles, check out these 15 Actors Who Almost Played Avengers and Actors Who Almost Played Batman .
items.title_en: The "Next James Bond" Actors Who Never Played James Bond

items.title: Former James Bond Actor George Lazenby Gives Robert Pattinson Advice After Batman Star Scores Iconic Role
items.excerpt: George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role.
items.content_text: George Lazenby, who formerly portrayed James Bond, is giving Robert Pattinson some sage advice after the Batman actor scored the historic and highly coveted role. After a lengthy and secretive casting process stacked with some of Britain’s greatest actors, Robert Pattinson was officially revealed as the next James Bond on November 16, 2026. This marks the latest in a string of high-profile parts Pattinson has played lately, which include Batman , Chris Hansen in Primetime , Antinous in Nolan’s Odyssey, and Scytale in Dune: Part Three. It’s safe to say that Pattinson is no stranger to being the face of a franchise, what with his experience playing Edward Cullen in the Twilight saga and Batman in Matt Reeves’ take on the caped crusader. But James Bond is a different beast entirely, as fans’ reactions to this latest news have already proven this fact. Luckily, he’s not alone. A slew of other actors have taken up the 007 mantle before him, including Lazenby, who portrayed the character in 1969's On Her Majesty’s Secret Service . Lazenby took the opportunity to give Pattinson some useful tips before he steps into M16. “I hear they've announced the new James Bond,” Lazenby wrote in a post shared on social media. “Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have [a] ‘This never happened to the other fella!’ moment. All the best, mate, George xx.” It’s safe to say Pattinson is already having one of those moments, given the energetic opinions we’ve seen on social media already. Many fans are ecstatic about him being cast as Bond, given his extensive filmography playing the tortured hero; others, however, aren’t so sure that he’s a good fit, while others are joking that he’s being too “greedy” by taking up all the best roles in Hollywood. I hear they've announced the new James Bond @007... Robert, welcome to the most exclusive club in the world. But remember to enjoy yourself. Let's see if you'll have "this never happened to the other fella" moment. All the best mate, George xx https://t.co/r0kASTyp35 — George Lazenby (@lazenbyofficial) November 16, 2026 It’s certainly been quite a year for Pattinson, who’s had a nice few films that have dominated the box office this year. He, along with Tom Holland and Zendaya, is one of the most recognizable faces in the business right now — and it proves how far he’s come from his days as Edward Cullen. In fact, Pattinson was apparently so coveted for Bond that he was reportedly offered a more lucrative contract for fewer films than other actors in the running, which included Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor, and Nicholas Hoult. For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Pattinson’s Bond has to offer. In the meantime, you can look forward to watching him in Dune: Part Three this December.

items.title: Subway Is Releasing a GTA 6-Themed Sandwich, but There's a Catch
items.excerpt: Subway is getting on the GTA 6 hype train with a sandwich themed after the highly anticipated game.
items.content_text: Subway is getting on the GTA 6 hype train with a sandwich themed after the highly anticipated game. The sandwich chain announced today that it is giving its Miami-exclusive Cubano Pulled Pork Melt a GTA 6 "reskin" in time for the new game. The sandwich is being renamed the Vice City Cubano and, as noted, is only available in the city of Miami. The sandwich comes either as a six-inch or footlong sub and features hardwood-smoked pulled pork, black forest ham, melted provolone, pickles, and mustard on freshly baked artisan Italian bread. Subway confirmed that the sandwich will be available both in-store and for delivery for those who don't plan to leave their couch when GTA 6 is released. You can see an image of it below. Subway isn't the only fast food place getting in on on the GTA 6 hype. Popeyes is also releasing a Vice City-themed chicken sandwich that it calls "Spice City." It will be available for one week starting November 19 and is available at participating locations for in-store pick up or delivery. Finally, there are also a bunch of Miami-based dining options and stores that have officially teamed up with Rockstar to provide themed meals and drinks based on GTA. The most notable of the bunch is a partnership with Skinny Louie, a burger chain based out of Florida. The chain has been turned into Burger Shot , a fast food joint prominently featured in the GTA franchise. The menu, uniforms, packaging, and signange for Skinny Louie has been completely refitted with Burger Shot branding, which will remain in place until the end of the year. Rockstar's marketing power has reached unprecedented levels, even prompting other places that don't have a partnership in place to try and ride the hype waves. GTA 6 will release this Thursday for Xbox Series X|S and PS5. Players can pre-load the game right now and they absolutely should, as the game is a whopping 210 GBs.

items.title: UK’s National Health Service Is Urging Gamers to Protect Their Hands Ahead of GTA 6 Launch
items.excerpt: The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19.
items.content_text: The UK’s National Health Service is giving players advice to help them avoid straining their hands once GTA 6 finally releases on November 19. The service’s humorous PSA was posted to Instagram on November 16, just three days before Rockstar’s highly anticipated game launches. The post includes several photos taken by the NHS’s social media manager, whose hand has been wrapped up tight in a cast. The poor employee explained that they underwent surgery to “remove a lump” from their hand, which they said is particularly “bad timing” due to GTA 6’s imminent release. To help others avoid injuring themselves and being unable to play, they shared some tips to keep your ligaments in tip-top shape. For starters, the NHS is urging players to “try and take regular breaks.” This helps avoid eye strain, and getting up from your gaming chair or sofa every couple of hours is good for circulation, relieving muscle stiffness, and providing mental clarity. (That’s right — you might actually play better if you take regular breaks.) The NHS’s post was particularly concerned with RSI, or repetitive strain injury, which it described as “pain that can be caused by repeated movement of part of the body, such as hands and fingers.” RSI can happen for a number of reasons; sports like tennis or golfing can be culprits, as can jobs like hairdressing (using scissors and other tools), working an assembly line, and even typing at your computer. While RSI is a general umbrella term for these types of injuries, carpal tunnel is a more specific condition that falls under the RSI label. Gamers are prone to this type of strain, due to pressing buttons quickly and repetitively, moving a joystick back and forth, and gripping one’s controller or mouse tightly while playing. While a repetitive strain injury might legitimately be something you could call out of work for, you might have a hard time getting the time off, given how many players are already planning on taking time off from their jobs to roam around Vice City. There's already been a 17% increase in time-off requests from employees for November 19, and even world governments like Germany and Australia are talking about the game’s upcoming impact on the workforce. In fact, estimates show that GTA 6 is likely to drain $1 billion from the US economy, since so many people will be staying at home to play on November 19. Some companies are getting a jump on the amount of ‘sick’ employees they’ll likely have by offering the time off ahead of time, with tech giant Logitech giving staff the option to take personal days for major video game releases. Just remember to take regular breaks — Vice City will be just fine without you for a few moments.

items.title: GTA 6 Gets New Screenshots Highlighting Leonida's Dynamic Weather
items.excerpt: Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather.
items.content_text: Rockstar has revealed a new batch of GTA 6 screenshots – and even a Weather Channel forecast – showcasing Leonida's dynamic weather. The 13-year wait for a proper return to Vice City is almost over, but with just days to go until launch, no one had any idea what to expect from the week. Would more details leak? Would Rockstar reveal more gameplay details? Would we get more gameplay footage? Either way, it's probably safe to say no one was expecting to check the forecast to find out the latest on GTA 6. The Weather Channel struck when it published a series of screenshots showing Vice City covered in everything from torrential downpours to ocean fog. We even get a true-to-life breakdown of what we're seeing here, giving would-be Leonida citizens a chance to prep before the storm hits. Heavy rain is kicking up a lot of moisture making visibility poor in many places in the Keys, luckily the local authorities have installed reflectors in some of the roads to help driving (better get your headlights fixed at Coastal Auto Care) https://t.co/tpCfXirjV0 — The Weather Channel (@weatherchannel) November 16, 2026 "Grand Theft Auto VI takes place in Leonida – a fictional world inspired by modern-day Florida, a landscape with one of the most unpredictable weather systems in the US," Rockstar VP of art: light and rendering Owen Shepherd said. "To match the fidelity of all aspects of what is the deepest, most immersive take on the Grand Theft Auto series yet, we had to completely reimagine our in-game weather systems to feel more localized, persistent, and above all dynamic. Weather can range with everything from clear blue skies to towering vertiginous cumulonimbus clouds, grounding players in a world through weather we hope Florida locals – and new visitors to Leonida – can appreciate." Rockstar confirmed it had developed an "advanced" weather system when speaking to Game Informer in September. items.title: Blizzard Tries 2 World of Warcraft Dungeon Fixes Over the Weekend to Stop Boosting Services
items.excerpt: World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to get to high enough levels to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.
items.content_text: World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to level up enough to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players. Over the weekend, Blizzard pushed out a November 13 hotfix that made it so if there's any player in a group that's too high of a level to earn experience from monsters, no one in that group gets experience. The goal seems to be to get rid of boosting, where one high-level player can carry a group of players through dungeons to level them up quickly. But that solution backfired. The problem is that in a lot of Forever's dungeons, there's a wide level range, so players on the high end of that range ended up accidentally nullifying everyone else's experience in the dungeon. That even happened to me on Saturday when trying to run Excavation Site with a level 37 player in my group. The next day, Blizzard admitted that hotfix went too far. On the WoW Forever forums, community manager Kaivax posted , saying, "Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon." Instead, Blizzard changed the way the restriction works. Rather than basing it on whether or not an enemy is "trivial" to any of the players, there's now a flat level difference restriction on experience. As Kaivax puts it, "We’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies." For those who are just trying to do dungeons as they naturally come up while questing, the latest update should completely fix the issue, while also preventing boosters from powering people through the game. After all, Blizzard is dead-set on encouraging players to level out in the world, and is apparently not afraid of using some heavy-handed tactics to do so. This also isn’t the first time that Blizzard has needed to adjust dungeon experience. Back when the WoW Forever beta first opened, the company severely limited the amount of XP you get from dungeons, only to buff it last week – even if it’s still far below what you’d earn in Classic . Blizzard has also changed the way gold is earned , in order to stop people from feeling like they had to hoard quest turn-ins for when they hit max level.

items.title: Austin Creed Goes Viral After Pulling Off Explosive Real-Life Shoryuken in AEW Full Gear Match
items.excerpt: Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm.
items.content_text: Pro wrestler Austin Creed went viral over the weekend for pulling off an iconic fighting game move in real life, hitting his opponent with an explosive Shoryuken in a viral moment that took social media by storm. Creed, alongside Kofi Kingston and Swerve Strickland, put on a stunning performance at AEW’s Full Gear event on Saturday, November 14. The trio took on Brody King, Hangman Page, and the masked Bandido for a 3v3 brawl that saw a number of props and weapons used in the fight, which are allowed by Texas Death Match rules. One of these props was a Nintendo Power Glove, an old-school accessory for the Nintendo Entertainment System that was first released in 1989. Of course, being a pro wrestling match, this particular Power Glove had special powers that allowed its wearer to pull off some especially brutal moves. Wake up ➡️⬇️↘️+👊🏾 https://t.co/lgJpD6oWy4 — Austin Creed (@AustinCreedWins) November 15, 2026 During his turn with King, Creed pulled the Power Glove out of a bag and slipped it on — but he took a tad too long, getting whacked in the head and sent to his knees. King smacked him a second time, seemingly outdoing his rival before Creed suddenly stood and hit him with a Shoryuken, his fist exploding in sparks and sending King flying backwards. The moment went viral within wrestling circles and the fighting game community. Players wasted no time joking about Creed’s “wakeup DP” and “reversal,” with legendary pro player Justin Wong comparing the move to Daigo Umehara’s famed “Umeshoryus.” To explain these terms to non-fighting gamers, a ‘DP’ refers to a Dragon Punch, which is a category of uppercut-style special move. ‘Wakeup’ is the moment that a player’s character recovers after being knocked down, while a ‘reversal’ refers to a player successfully executing a move and striking the opposing character as soon as possible after being hit. In essence, Creed hit King with a reversal DP on wakeup — a move that King probably should have seen coming. “Lmao he just stayed still without blocking on his wakeup, deserved to get hit by reversal DP,” prominent fighting game YouTuber Rooflemonger joked . “This is the coldest thing I've seen in the ring in over two decades,” game artist CartelDel remarked . “Totally invincible on frames 1-8,” another teased . Creed is one of several pro wrestlers who have referenced fighting games in the ring; Kenny Omega famously uses moves like Street Fighter 5 ’s V-Trigger against his opponents, and even contributed to Alex’s moveset for Street Fighter 6. Cody Rhodes, who famously portrayed Guile in the 2026 Street Fighter movie , also showed up to WWE Summer Slam in full Guile attire — including the character’s iconic flat-top hairstyle.

A 39" monitor is pretty wide, so the AW3926QW employs a 1500R curve to balance it out. 1500R is pretty moderate as far as curved monitors go, so although you'll be able to see the entire monitor within your field of view, it won't significantly distort peripheral images. OLED monitors are known for their extreme fast response time and perfect black levels, making them ideal for gaming. It has both DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 ports so you'll be able to connect it to just about any modern day graphics card without the need for adapters. items.title: Nvidia Reportedly Uninterested in Bringing Jensen Huang Back as CEO
items.excerpt: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
items.content_text: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement. The latest turn in the tech giant's whirlwind week arrived yesterday, when the Financial Times reported that the company's ex-boss had supported efforts from his friends in Silicon Valley to see him brought back into the fold . One source said these allies had assembled a "war room" to lay the foundation for his return, but it now seems those efforts may have been for naught. The Nvidia board of directors is not considering reinstating Huang as CEO after he resigned from his position Thursday, November 12, one source told CNBC . Instead, company leadership is focused on the ongoing investigation launched after Huang confirmed he had an affair with a woman whom members of the U.S. government believed to be a Chinese spy on November 8. The report states Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to look into his relationship with the individual and how it may have compromised company secrets and/or national security. A message from the board added it had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" when announcing the investigation last week. One of the supposed goals of Huang's secret war room of Silicon Valley supporters was to gain White House support for the reinstatement – and it's a plan that seems to have panned out. U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters today (via Bloomberg ) that he "would not mind" seeing the embattled tech leader return. "I would not mind. I would not mind that," he said. "I threw out the name of Tim Cook , but I would say that Jensen's reinstatement… I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson's more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that." Huang and Nvidia are now trying to pick up the pieces after the investigation began last week. The story so far has seen tech billionaire Elon Musk publicly back Huang , with some Nvidia employees saying they'd like him reinstated, too. Additional reports have said the former CEO had additional affairs with not one but two of his subordinates . Photo by Nadja Wohlleben/Getty Images.

items.title: Why Robert Pattinson Likely Can’t Play Batman and James Bond Together
items.excerpt: Robert Pattinson taking on the James Bond role probably means that The Batman: Part II is his final outing as the Dark Knight. Here's why Pattinson likely can't (or won't) play both roles going forward.
items.content_text: Our long international nightmare is finally over. Amazon MGM Studios has selected a new actor to play James Bond, and it’s none other than former Twilight star Robert Pattinson . Despite being an actor who tends to prioritize quirky indie roles (while throwing in the occasional blockbuster for good measure), Pattinson has signed on to star in another of the film world’s biggest franchises. This means Pattinson will now be in the unique position of playing both Batman and Bond. But can that arrangement last long-term, or is this a sign that the actor's days in Gotham City are coming to an end? Unfortunately, we think the latter possibility is the more likely one. Here’s why Pattinson is probably trading one superhero role for another, and why The Batman: Part II is almost certainly the end of the road for that particular series. Robert Pattinson: From Batman to Bond Pattinson’s Bond casting is certainly an interesting and unexpected development. MGM has tended to focus on up-and-coming actors for the various Bond films, whether it was a then little-known Sean Connery in 1962’s Dr. No or Daniel Craig in 2006’s Casino Royale. Early on, it seemed Amazon was going to continue operating under this philosophy , with relatively lesser-known actors like Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor emerging as frontrunners. Apparently, the studio had a change of heart. Compared to past Bonds, Pattinson is already a huge name with a wide resume and multiple key franchises under his belt. This is basically like if the studio hired Christian Bale to take on the Bond role after 2005’s Batman Begins. It’s a lot of cinematic responsibility for one actor to shoulder. Is there a world where Pattinson continues to juggle the dual responsibilities of playing Batman and Bond? Perhaps. The actor certainly seems to like keeping busy as an actor. In 2026 alone, he’s starred in The Drama, The Odyssey, and Primetime, and we still have his sci-fi heel turn in Dune: Part 3 coming up in December. Still, it seems unlikely that even an actor as prolific as Pattinson is able or willing to juggle both James Bond and Bruce Wayne at the same time. Again, both roles are massive responsibilities that each require a huge time commitment, including the massive promotional push that comes after filming has wrapped. Look at what happened to Mahershala Ali when he signed on to do Blade for Marvel Studios. Even though that project never came to be, Ali had to turn down a lot of work because he was so focused on training for the role and developing the film. Or look at Xochitl Gomez, who basically stopped getting offers after appearing in 2022’s Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness because casting agents assumed she was too tied up in the Marvel machine. Being James Bond and being Batman are both comparable. Each role can keep the actor tied up for months or years at a time. The odds that one franchise might interfere with the other in the years ahead seem rather high. With many years already having passed since 2021’s No Time to Die, Amazon MGM likely wants to push forward quickly with the reboot. We highly doubt an actor like Pattinson, who clearly values his freedom to pursue interesting and unusual projects in this post-Twilight phase of his career, has any real desire to attempt to juggle both Batman and Bond simultaneously. This Bond news simply signals the idea that Pattinson feels his days as Batman are coming to an end. Currently, Steven Soderbergh has stepped in to finish production on The Batman: Part II while Matt Reeves deals with a personal matter. Once that wraps in late 2026 or early 2027, we’re guessing Pattinson will most likely hang up the cape and cowl and move on to other projects, one of which is the long-awaited James Bond reboot. He’s just trading one blockbuster franchise for another. The Problem With Matt Reeves’ Batman Universe Mind you, Pattinson may not be moving on from Batman out of a waning interest in the character, but simply due to the reality on the ground. There’s a lot currently working against this iteration of the Batman franchise. As mentioned, director Matt Reeves has had to step away from production due to personal problems. It’s unclear how heavy a role Reeves will have in the film’s post-production. We’re sure a third movie isn’t high on his list of priorities at the moment. The likelihood is that if the newly merged Skydance even wants a The Batman: Part III, they’d have to push forward without Reeves as writer or director if they don’t want another long gap between sequels. Do fans actually want a Reeves-less The Batman: Part III? Would Pattinson even be interested in returning in that eventuality? Losing this series’ defining creative voice seems like too big a hurdle to cross. And that’s assuming Skydance wants The Batman: Part III to happen at all. Right now, we have no idea what direction they’re taking with the DC line after firing James Gunn and Peter Safran. We’d argue the current DCU continuity should stay in place , but there’s no guarantee that’ll happen. All we can say for sure is that Batman, easily the most bankable DC character in existence, is going to be a major priority for the studio going forward. It stands to reason that executives aren’t thrilled with how long it’s taken to put out a sequel to 2022’s The Batman. And they’re probably also not fond of the fact that Reeves’ The Batman movies exist in their own little universe, while the Batman of Gunn and Safran’s DCU is still an enigma after all these years. Historically, DC has always shied away from allowing multiple incarnations of characters to coexist in live-action, and that approach may continue under Skydance. That leaves Skydance with two options - either focus on the Pattinson/Reeves universe as the sole Batman going forward, or reboot the character and pivot to something relatively more family-friendly and with more box office potential. That leaves Skydance with two options - either focus on the Pattinson/Reeves universe as the sole Batman going forward, or reboot the character and pivot to something relatively more family-friendly and with more box office potential. We tend to think the company would opt for the latter. Incoming DC Studios head Jeremy Latcham seems to prefer more uplifting and family-friendly movies, and it would be in keeping with Paramount’s recent approach to the TMNT franchise . Basically, between Reeves’ ongoing personal problems and the general direction of the wind at Skydance, there’s a good chance that there’s no future for the “ Batman Epic Crime Saga ” after The Batman: Part II finally arrives in 2028. We’re not holding our breath for The Penguin Season 2 either. That’s likely why Pattinson agreed to play James Bond. He sees the writing on the wall for his version of Batman, and he’s moving on to greener pastures. It’s a shame in many ways, but we suspect that Skydance’s loss will be Amazon MGM’s gain in the years to come. Pattinson may not be the most bold or exciting choice to play Bond, but we can’t imagine he won’t do well in the role. There are far worse outcomes for this venerable franchise than to have Pattinson and director Denis Villeneuve rebooting it for a new era.
